The invention relates to a chain guide or chain tensioner intended for use in a lubricated sliding system, particularly in applications where a moving chain is guided, supported, or tensioned while operating in contact with a sliding surface. Such components are commonly used in power train drive systems, for example in engine timing systems or other chain-driven mechanical assemblies in which reliable operation, low friction, and durability at elevated temperatures are required.

The chain guide, chain tensioner, or associated sliding element comprises a surface layer that is primarily formed from a polymeric material. This surface layer provides the contact surface against which the chain slides during operation. By selecting an appropriate polymeric material for this layer, the sliding element can achieve reduced friction, improved wear resistance, and stable mechanical performance under lubricated operating conditions.

The polymeric material includes a matrix polymer made of a semi-crystalline polyamide. This semi-crystalline polyamide is selected such that it has a tensile modulus at 140° C. of at least 800 MPa. The relatively high tensile modulus at elevated temperature ensures that the sliding surface retains sufficient stiffness and dimensional stability during operation, even under the thermal and mechanical loads typically encountered in lubricated chain drive systems.

The invention also extends to a power train drive system comprising a lubricated drive chain and at least one plastic sliding component positioned in sliding contact with the chain. The plastic sliding component may be, for example, a chain guide, a chain tensioner shoe, or another sliding element arranged to guide or tension the chain as it moves. The lubricating oil present in the system reduces wear and assists in heat dissipation, while the specially selected polymeric surface layer further contributes to low-friction performance.

In particular, the sliding element is characterized by a coefficient of friction of at most 0.07 when measured under specified lubricated test conditions. These conditions include measurement in lubrication oil at a temperature of 140° C., under a nominal contact pressure of 1 MPa, and at a sliding speed of 1 m/s. Achieving such a low coefficient of friction under these demanding conditions indicates that the sliding element is well suited for high-temperature, lubricated chain applications, offering reduced energy losses, lower wear, and improved efficiency of the overall drive system.
outputs.L4:
A chain guide or chain tensioner is provided for use in lubricated sliding systems, particularly in drive systems exposed to elevated operating temperatures. The component includes a sliding element having a surface layer that comes into contact with a moving chain, belt, or similar transmission member. This surface layer is formed primarily from a semi-crystalline polyamide matrix polymer, selected for its high mechanical strength and dimensional stability under hot operating conditions. In particular, the polymer has a high tensile modulus at 140°C, allowing the sliding element to maintain rigidity, wear resistance, and reliable guiding performance even when continuously exposed to heated lubricant.

The material composition of the surface layer is designed to provide excellent tribological behavior in hot lubrication oil. When used in an oil-lubricated environment, such as an internal combustion engine or another power train application, the sliding element exhibits a very low coefficient of friction against the chain or other moving component. This reduced friction helps limit energy losses, lower heat generation, and minimize wear on both the sliding element and the chain. As a result, the chain guide or chain tensioner offers improved durability, reduced operating noise, and enhanced efficiency.

Because of these properties, the described sliding element is especially suitable for demanding power train drive systems, including timing chain drives, balance shaft drives, oil pump drives, and other chain-driven assemblies. The combination of a semi-crystalline polyamide matrix with high stiffness at elevated temperature and low-friction performance in lubricating oil enables reliable operation over long service intervals. This makes the component well suited for modern engine and transmission systems where reduced friction, long-term wear resistance, and stable performance under high-temperature lubrication conditions are required.

The SCPA is a concept or system that can be discussed in relation to pressure, performance, and material strength. In many technical fields, pressure is measured in MPa, which stands for megapascals. One MPa equals one million pascals and is commonly used in engineering, construction, manufacturing, and scientific testing.

The SCPA may involve processes where pressure levels are important for safety, efficiency, or quality control. For example, if a material or device is tested under a pressure of several MPa, engineers can evaluate how well it performs under demanding conditions. This helps ensure that the system remains reliable and meets required standards.

Understanding the relationship between the SCPA and MPa measurements is essential for accurate analysis. The use of MPa provides a clear and standardized way to describe pressure, making it easier for professionals to compare results, design safe systems, and improve overall performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an invention summary for a lubricated drive chain system using a plastic sliding element, where the matrix polymer is SCPA with high-temperature modulus and low CoF under defined test conditions.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

The invention relates to a lubricated drive chain system comprising a circulating drive chain and at least one plastic sliding element arranged to guide, tension, support, or damp the drive chain during operation. The sliding element includes a polymeric sliding body formed from a matrix polymer comprising SCPA, preferably a semi-crystalline polyamide, selected to provide improved tribological performance in lubricated chain-contact applications.

In one aspect, the SCPA matrix polymer is characterized by a high-temperature mechanical stiffness and a low coefficient of friction under defined test conditions. In particular, the SCPA matrix polymer has a tensile or flexural modulus at elevated temperature sufficient to maintain dimensional stability and contact geometry under chain loading, for example at temperatures representative of engine, transmission, or industrial drive operation. The SCPA matrix polymer further exhibits a low coefficient of friction when tested against a metallic chain-contact counterface under lubricated conditions, thereby reducing sliding losses, wear, heat generation, and noise.

The plastic sliding element may be configured as a chain guide, chain rail, tensioner shoe, guide shoe, sprocket-adjacent sliding member, or other chain-contact component. The sliding surface is positioned to contact link plates, rollers, pins, bushings, or other portions of the drive chain in the presence of a lubricant such as oil, grease, or a circulating lubrication medium. The use of the SCPA matrix polymer enables the sliding element to withstand elevated operating temperatures while maintaining a low-friction interface with the moving chain.

In certain embodiments, the SCPA matrix polymer has a high-temperature modulus measured at an elevated temperature, such as about 120°C to about 180°C, and a coefficient of friction measured under lubricated sliding contact against steel under a specified load, speed, temperature, and lubricant condition. The SCPA may be used alone or in combination with additives, reinforcements, fillers, solid lubricants, wear modifiers, heat stabilizers, or impact modifiers. Suitable additives may include glass fibers, carbon fibers, aramid fibers, graphite, PTFE, molybdenum disulfide, silicone-based modifiers, mineral fillers, or combinations thereof, provided that the sliding element retains the desired high-temperature modulus and low-friction behavior.

The lubricated drive chain system provides improved durability and efficiency compared with conventional chain systems using sliding elements made from lower-temperature or higher-friction polymers. By combining a lubricated metal chain with a plastic sliding element based on an SCPA matrix polymer, the system can reduce chain guide wear, maintain chain alignment, improve tension control, decrease frictional power loss, and extend service life in high-temperature operating environments.

In an exemplary embodiment, the drive chain system includes a metal timing chain operating in an oil-lubricated environment and a chain guide having a sliding surface molded from an SCPA-based composition. The SCPA-based composition exhibits a high modulus at elevated temperature and a low coefficient of friction under lubricated steel-contact testing, allowing the guide to maintain structural integrity and provide low-resistance sliding contact throughout prolonged operation.

Thus, the invention provides a lubricated drive chain system in which the plastic sliding element is specifically engineered from an SCPA matrix polymer having defined high-temperature stiffness and lubricated low-friction properties, resulting in a robust, low-wear, and energy-efficient chain guidance system.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a European patent application paragraph for a chain guide or chain tensioner comprising a polymeric surface layer, including ISO 527-1A tensile modulus requirements and lubrication-oil friction measurements.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, the chain guide or chain tensioner comprises a support body and a polymeric surface layer arranged on a chain-sliding surface of the support body, the polymeric surface layer being adapted to contact a chain during operation in the presence of lubricating oil. The polymeric surface layer is formed from a polymer composition having a tensile modulus of at least 1,500 MPa, preferably from 2,000 MPa to 8,000 MPa, as determined in accordance with ISO 527 using a type 1A test specimen according to ISO 527-1A at 23°C. The polymer composition is further selected such that, when a test piece of the polymeric surface layer is tested against a steel counter body under lubrication with engine oil at 100°C, the coefficient of sliding friction is not greater than 0.12, preferably not greater than 0.08, as measured in a reciprocating or pin-on-disc friction test at a normal load of 50 N and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s. By combining the specified tensile modulus with the defined oil-lubricated friction behaviour, the polymeric surface layer provides sufficient stiffness and wear resistance while reducing frictional losses and noise during chain operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an automotive powertrain drive system invention involving an engine, transmission differential, drive shaft, drive chain, and a plastic sliding component made mainly of semi-crystalline polyamide.
counterfactuals.output:
An automotive powertrain drive system comprises an internal combustion engine, a transmission differential unit, a drive shaft for transmitting torque from the differential to a driven wheel, and a drive chain arranged in the powertrain to transmit rotational power between sprockets. The drive chain is guided, supported, or tensioned by a sliding component that is in direct sliding contact with the chain during operation.

The sliding component may be formed as a chain guide, chain shoe, tensioner shoe, rail, or wear strip. It is made primarily from a semi-crystalline polyamide resin, such as PA6, PA66, PA46, PA610, PA612, PA11, PA12, or a copolyamide/blend having a semi-crystalline structure. The material may optionally include reinforcing fibers, solid lubricants, impact modifiers, heat stabilizers, wear-resistant additives, or fillers to improve dimensional stability, friction behavior, heat resistance, and durability.

In operation, torque produced by the engine is delivered through the transmission differential and into the drive shaft. The drive chain transfers rotation within the drivetrain, while the plastic sliding component maintains proper chain path and tension and reduces noise, vibration, and wear. Because the sliding component is mainly semi-crystalline polyamide, it provides a favorable balance of low friction, abrasion resistance, mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, oil resistance, and thermal stability, making it suitable for prolonged use in an automotive powertrain environment.

The invention therefore provides a lightweight, durable, and low-noise chain-guiding structure for an engine-driven automotive drivetrain including a transmission differential, drive shaft, and drive chain.
